note: After the revision by Constantino (1995); the original is in English. Alates, soldiers and workers are described. The original gives only the measurements of the holotype female alate (mm): head length (to mandible base) 3.2, head width 3.47, fontanelle length 0.33, pronotum length 2.27, pronotum width 4.2, hind tibia length 5.2, maximum diameter of the compound eye 1.2, ocellus length 0.4; soldier measurements were not available for this entry (the relevant OCR pages are missing or garbled). The original description by Snyder (1924) is the basis for the type locality.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate appears indistinguishable from S. grandis. The soldier is distinguished by its large size, the large marginal teeth on the mandibles, the evenly curved apical cutting edges and the relatively short thoracic spines.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes large, more than 1/3 of the head width; ocelli large; fontanelle round and relatively small. Antennae 20-segmented. Anterior corners of the pronotum moderately angular; lateral margins straight, nearly parallel on the anterior half. Wings long; apex of the mediana and cubitus indistinct. Head capsule and postclypeus with numerous long setae (many have been lost in the type specimens); outer margin and surface of the pronotum hairy; abdominal tergites hairy from the middle to the posterior margin. Head, pronotum and abdominal tergites dark brown; sternites pale chestnut.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule short, head length and width subequal; sides contracted anteriorly; posterior margin of the head round. Frontal tube very short, the pore clearly visible in dorsal view. Labrum short, length and width subequal; lateral angles about equal to or slightly greater than a right angle; midlobe of medium size.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Worker: head capsule with numerous short, straight setae; postclypeus with about 10 setae; fontanelle slightly elongate and relatively small. Spines of the thoracic nota weak. Mandibles and hind gut very similar to S. obtusus, the molar plate of the right mandible broad.
